import Mathlib

structure BinaryMaxHeap where
  storage : List Int
deriving Inhabited

namespace BinaryMaxHeap

def len (h : BinaryMaxHeap) : Nat :=
  h.storage.length

def get (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (i : Nat) : Int :=
  h.storage.getD i 0 -- Safe access with default

def parent (i : Nat) : Nat := (i - 1) / 2

def is_heap (h : BinaryMaxHeap) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, 0 < i ∧ i < h.len → h.get i ≤ h.get (parent i)

def view (h : BinaryMaxHeap) : Multiset Int :=
  Multiset.ofList h.storage

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def push_precond (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_heap h ∧ h.len < 1023 -- Limited capacity as per spec example
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Swap the entries at positions `i` and `j`. -/
def swapAt (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) : List Int :=
  (l.set i (l.getD j 0)).set j (l.getD i 0)

/-- Bubble the element at position `i` up towards the root. -/
def siftUp (l : List Int) (i : Nat) : List Int :=
  if _h : 0 < i then
    if l.getD ((i - 1) / 2) 0 < l.getD i 0 then
      siftUp (swapAt l i ((i - 1) / 2)) ((i - 1) / 2)
    else l
  else l
termination_by i
decreasing_by omega

/-- The heap invariant, stated directly on the underlying list. -/
def IsHeapList (l : List Int) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, 0 < j → j < l.length → l.getD j 0 ≤ l.getD ((j - 1) / 2) 0

/-- Invariant maintained by `siftUp`: the list is a heap except possibly at `i`,
whose value may be too large; moreover the children of `i` are already bounded by
the value sitting at the parent of `i` (which is what will be moved into `i`). -/
def SiftInv (l : List Int) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ j, 0 < j → j < l.length → j ≠ i → l.getD j 0 ≤ l.getD ((j - 1) / 2) 0) ∧
  (∀ c, 0 < c → c < l.length → (c - 1) / 2 = i → l.getD c 0 ≤ l.getD ((i - 1) / 2) 0)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def push (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : push_precond h v) : BinaryMaxHeap :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  ⟨siftUp (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length⟩
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def push_postcond (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int) (result : BinaryMaxHeap)
    (_ : push_precond h v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_heap result ∧
  result.len = h.len + 1 ∧
  result.view = h.view + {v}
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
lemma getD_set_self' (l : List Int) (i : Nat) (a : Int) (hi : i < l.length) :
    (l.set i a).getD i 0 = a := by
  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, hi]

lemma getD_set_of_ne (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) (a : Int) (hij : j ≠ i) :
    (l.set i a).getD j 0 = l.getD j 0 := by
  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, Ne.symm hij]

lemma getD_append_lt (l₁ l₂ : List Int) (j : Nat) (hj : j < l₁.length) :
    (l₁ ++ l₂).getD j 0 = l₁.getD j 0 := by
  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_append_left hj]

lemma swapAt_length (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) : (swapAt l i j).length = l.length := by
  simp [swapAt]

lemma swapAt_get_fst (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) (hij : i ≠ j) (hi : i < l.length) :
    (swapAt l i j).getD i 0 = l.getD j 0 := by
  rw [swapAt, getD_set_of_ne _ _ _ _ hij, getD_set_self' _ _ _ hi]

lemma swapAt_get_snd (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) (hj : j < l.length) :
    (swapAt l i j).getD j 0 = l.getD i 0 := by
  rw [swapAt, getD_set_self' _ _ _ (by simpa using hj)]

lemma swapAt_get_other (l : List Int) (i j k : Nat) (hki : k ≠ i) (hkj : k ≠ j) :
    (swapAt l i j).getD k 0 = l.getD k 0 := by
  rw [swapAt, getD_set_of_ne _ _ _ _ hkj, getD_set_of_ne _ _ _ _ hki]

/-- Overwriting position `i` with `a` replaces the old entry by `a`. -/
lemma ofList_set (l : List Int) (i : Nat) (a : Int) (hi : i < l.length) :
    (Multiset.ofList (l.set i a)) + {l.getD i 0} = (Multiset.ofList l) + {a} := by
  induction l generalizing i with
  | nil => simp at hi
  | cons x t ih =>
    match i with
    | 0 =>
      show (Multiset.ofList (a :: t)) + {x} = (Multiset.ofList (x :: t)) + {a}
      rw [← Multiset.cons_coe, ← Multiset.cons_coe, Multiset.cons_add, Multiset.cons_add,
        add_comm (Multiset.ofList t) {x}, add_comm (Multiset.ofList t) {a},
        Multiset.singleton_add, Multiset.singleton_add, Multiset.cons_swap]
    | k + 1 =>
      have hk : k < t.length := by simpa using hi
      show (Multiset.ofList (x :: t.set k a)) + {t.getD k 0}
          = (Multiset.ofList (x :: t)) + {a}
      rw [← Multiset.cons_coe, ← Multiset.cons_coe, Multiset.cons_add, Multiset.cons_add,
        ih k hk]

lemma ofList_swapAt (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) (hi : i < l.length) (hj : j < l.length) :
    Multiset.ofList (swapAt l i j) = Multiset.ofList l := by
  have hmid : (l.set i (l.getD j 0)).getD j 0 = l.getD j 0 := by
    by_cases hij : j = i
    · subst hij; exact getD_set_self' _ _ _ hi
    · exact getD_set_of_ne _ _ _ _ hij
  have h1 := ofList_set l i (l.getD j 0) hi
  have h2 := ofList_set (l.set i (l.getD j 0)) j (l.getD i 0) (by simpa using hj)
  rw [hmid, h1] at h2
  exact add_right_cancel h2

lemma siftUp_length : ∀ (i : Nat) (l : List Int), (siftUp l i).length = l.length := by
  intro i
  induction i using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ i ih =>
    intro l
    rw [siftUp]
    by_cases h0 : 0 < i
    · rw [dif_pos h0]
      by_cases hlt : l.getD ((i - 1) / 2) 0 < l.getD i 0
      · rw [if_pos hlt, ih ((i - 1) / 2) (by omega), swapAt_length]
      · rw [if_neg hlt]
    · rw [dif_neg h0]

lemma siftUp_multiset : ∀ (i : Nat) (l : List Int), i < l.length →
    Multiset.ofList (siftUp l i) = Multiset.ofList l := by
  intro i
  induction i using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ i ih =>
    intro l hi
    rw [siftUp]
    by_cases h0 : 0 < i
    · rw [dif_pos h0]
      by_cases hlt : l.getD ((i - 1) / 2) 0 < l.getD i 0
      · rw [if_pos hlt,
          ih ((i - 1) / 2) (by omega) _ (by rw [swapAt_length]; omega)]
        exact ofList_swapAt l i ((i - 1) / 2) hi (by omega)
      · rw [if_neg hlt]
    · rw [dif_neg h0]

lemma siftUp_heap : ∀ (i : Nat) (l : List Int), i < l.length → SiftInv l i →
    IsHeapList (siftUp l i) := by
  intro i
  induction i using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ i ih =>
    intro l hi hinv
    obtain ⟨hA, hB⟩ := hinv
    rw [siftUp]
    by_cases h0 : 0 < i
    · rw [dif_pos h0]
      by_cases hlt : l.getD ((i - 1) / 2) 0 < l.getD i 0
      · rw [if_pos hlt]
        have hpi : (i - 1) / 2 < i := by omega
        have hpl : (i - 1) / 2 < l.length := by omega
        have hine : i ≠ (i - 1) / 2 := by omega
        refine ih ((i - 1) / 2) hpi _ (by rw [swapAt_length]; omega) ⟨?_, ?_⟩
        · -- heap property away from the new focus `(i-1)/2`
          intro j hj0 hjl hjne
          rw [swapAt_length] at hjl
          by_cases hji : j = i
          · subst hji
            rw [swapAt_get_fst _ _ _ hine hi, swapAt_get_snd _ _ _ hpl]
            exact hlt.le
          · rw [swapAt_get_other l i ((i - 1) / 2) j hji hjne]
            by_cases hqi : (j - 1) / 2 = i
            · rw [hqi, swapAt_get_fst _ _ _ hine hi]
              exact hB j hj0 hjl hqi
            · by_cases hqp : (j - 1) / 2 = (i - 1) / 2
              · rw [hqp, swapAt_get_snd _ _ _ hpl]
                have h1 := hA j hj0 hjl hji
                rw [hqp] at h1
                exact le_trans h1 hlt.le
              · rw [swapAt_get_other l i ((i - 1) / 2) _ hqi hqp]
                exact hA j hj0 hjl hji
        · -- the children of the new focus are bounded by its parent's value
          intro c hc0 hcl hcp
          rw [swapAt_length] at hcl
          have hcnep : c ≠ (i - 1) / 2 := by omega
          by_cases hp0 : 0 < (i - 1) / 2
          · have hgi : ((i - 1) / 2 - 1) / 2 ≠ i := by omega
            have hgp : ((i - 1) / 2 - 1) / 2 ≠ (i - 1) / 2 := by omega
            rw [swapAt_get_other l i ((i - 1) / 2) _ hgi hgp]
            have hpar := hA ((i - 1) / 2) hp0 hpl (Ne.symm hine)
            by_cases hci : c = i
            · subst hci
              rw [swapAt_get_fst _ _ _ hine hi]
              exact hpar
            · rw [swapAt_get_other l i ((i - 1) / 2) c hci hcnep]
              have h1 := hA c hc0 hcl hci
              rw [hcp] at h1
              exact le_trans h1 hpar
          · have hg0 : ((i - 1) / 2 - 1) / 2 = (i - 1) / 2 := by omega
            rw [hg0, swapAt_get_snd _ _ _ hpl]
            by_cases hci : c = i
            · subst hci
              rw [swapAt_get_fst _ _ _ hine hi]
              exact hlt.le
            · rw [swapAt_get_other l i ((i - 1) / 2) c hci hcnep]
              have h1 := hA c hc0 hcl hci
              rw [hcp] at h1
              exact le_trans h1 hlt.le
      · rw [if_neg hlt]
        intro j hj0 hjl
        by_cases hji : j = i
        · subst hji
          exact not_lt.mp hlt
        · exact hA j hj0 hjl hji
    · rw [dif_neg h0]
      intro j hj0 hjl
      exact hA j hj0 hjl (by omega)
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem push_postcond_satisfied (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : push_precond h v) :
    push_postcond h v (push h v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  obtain ⟨hheap, -⟩ := h_precond
  have hLlen : (h.storage ++ [v]).length = h.storage.length + 1 := by simp
  have hnL : h.storage.length < (h.storage ++ [v]).length := by omega
  have hinv : SiftInv (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length := by
    constructor
    · intro j hj0 hjl hjne
      rw [hLlen] at hjl
      have hjlt : j < h.storage.length := by omega
      have hqlt : (j - 1) / 2 < h.storage.length := by omega
      rw [getD_append_lt _ _ _ hjlt, getD_append_lt _ _ _ hqlt]
      exact hheap j ⟨hj0, hjlt⟩
    · intro c hc0 hcl hcp
      rw [hLlen] at hcl
      omega
  have hres := siftUp_heap h.storage.length (h.storage ++ [v]) hnL hinv
  have hlen := siftUp_length h.storage.length (h.storage ++ [v])
  have hmul := siftUp_multiset h.storage.length (h.storage ++ [v]) hnL
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro j hj
    exact hres j hj.1 hj.2
  · show (siftUp (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length).length = h.storage.length + 1
    rw [hlen, hLlen]
  · show Multiset.ofList (siftUp (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length)
        = Multiset.ofList h.storage + {v}
    rw [hmul]
    rfl
  -- !benchmark @end proof

end BinaryMaxHeap

**LEAN VERIFIED** — `Solution.lean` compiles with no errors and no `sorry` (the two remaining warnings are about unused binders in the given, unmodified signatures).

## What I implemented

`push h v = ⟨siftUp (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length⟩` — a genuine append-then-bubble-up, not a re-sort. `siftUp l i` compares `l[i]` with `l[(i-1)/2]`, swaps and recurses on the parent while the child is strictly larger; it terminates because `(i-1)/2 < i` when `i > 0`.

## Key idea in the proof

The obvious invariant ("a heap everywhere except possibly at `i`") is **not** inductive. After swapping `i` with its parent `p`, position `i` receives the *smaller* value `l[p]`, and a child `c` of `i` only gives you `l[c] ≤ l[i]` — the wrong direction. So `SiftInv l i` carries a second clause:

- **(A)** every `j ≠ i` satisfies `l[j] ≤ l[parent j]`;
- **(B)** every child `c` of `i` satisfies `l[c] ≤ l[parent i]` — i.e. the subtree under `i` survives the incoming parent value.

Both endpoints then fall out cleanly: at the start `i = n` is the freshly appended slot, whose children are out of range, so (B) is vacuous; and when the recursion stops at `i = 0`, clause (A) *is* the heap property, since `j ≠ 0` is automatic for `j > 0`. The step lemma re-establishes both clauses for `p`, splitting on whether `p = 0` (where `parent p = p` and the grandparent slot coincides with the swapped one).

Supporting pieces: `getD`/`set` access lemmas, `ofList_set` (`↑(l.set i a) + {l[i]} = ↑l + {a}`, an addition-only form that dodges multiset subtraction) proved by induction, and `ofList_swapAt` obtained from it by cancellation — giving multiset preservation, with length preservation and the heap property each by strong induction on `i`.

What the natural language requires:
- insert the new value at the end,
- bubble it up,
- preserve heap property,
- size increases by 1,
- multiset/view gains exactly the new element.

What the student implemented:
- `push` is
  `⟨siftUp (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length⟩`
- This clearly appends `v` to the end of the underlying list.
- Then it calls `siftUp` starting from the old length, which is exactly the index of the newly inserted element.
- `siftUp` compares the element with its parent and swaps upward recursively while the parent is smaller. That is the standard bubble-up procedure for a max-heap.

This is the correct algorithmic approach requested by the problem. It is not some other heap operation, not a different algorithm, and not a call to a built-in heap library.
